intro.heading: Same market. Different zoom levels.
intro.body: The 1 minute, 5 minute, 1 hour, and 4 hour are not different markets — they are different views of the same price story. Lower timeframes show more detail. Higher timeframes show more direction.
intro.dayliNote: Timeframes change your perspective on the same market. The market itself never changes just because you switched the chart view.

chart.heading: Zoom through the timeframes
chart.prompt: Tap each lens to see how candle density changes at different zoom levels.

tapCards.prompt: Which timeframe would you check first to understand the bigger picture: 4H or 1M?

options.label: 4H
options.feedback: Right — higher timeframes are built to show the bigger directional story first.

options.label: 1M
options.feedback: The 1M is far too zoomed-in to establish the bigger picture on its own.

tapCards.prompt: You've read the 4H and have a directional bias. What's the next zoom level down usually used for?

options.label: Narrowing down to more specific structure and levels within that bigger picture
options.feedback: Right — each zoom level narrows the picture, it doesn't replace the one before it.

options.label: Throwing out the 4H read entirely and starting over
options.feedback: Lower timeframes build on the higher-timeframe read.

tapCards.prompt: You open the 1M and it looks messy, contradicting nothing you saw on the 4H. Should the 1M's messiness change your 4H bias?

options.label: No — the 1M is a detail view; messiness there doesn't erase a clear higher-timeframe read
options.feedback: Right — each timeframe answers a different question.

options.label: Yes — always trust whichever timeframe you're looking at right now
options.feedback: That would mean discarding useful context every time you zoom in.

quiz.question: What actually changes when you switch timeframes?
options: Your perspective on the same market
quiz.explanation: Timeframe changes your view — the underlying price story stays the same.

quiz.question: A trader checks the 1M chart first, decides it looks bullish, and takes a long without ever looking at the 4H. What is she missing?
options: The bigger-picture context the 4H would have given her about the larger direction
Nothing — the 1M is always sufficient on its own
The 1M is more reliable than any higher timeframe
quiz.explanation: The 1M can look convincing while running counter to the larger story the 4H reveals.

quiz.question: The clean workflow is higher timeframe first, then ___, then the lowest timeframe for entry detail.
quiz.explanation: Structure narrows the picture between the big-picture read and the entry detail.
